Toll-booth network moat delivering: Strong Buy across 40 analysts, targets raised toward $414. $2.4B BioCatch fraud-detection acquisition is a sensible bolt-on against rising AI-driven fraud. Hold size, no change to a working thesis.

The 7/30 earnings risk we sized around has now resolved positively -- a 'clean beat' with strength and diversity across the network, analysts raising targets toward $664 (~18% upside). Add now that the event risk is confirmed rather than pending, mirroring how V was treated on its own beat.
Membership moat intact -- July net sales $23.1B (+10.7% YoY), comps +8.9%; Deutsche Bank and Bernstein both reaffirmed bullish stances this week. Hold size.

Turnaround thesis still confirmed by the Q2 beat-and-raise; stock has pulled back modestly off its post-earnings high but analyst targets ($475+ consensus, some as high as $516-529) are unchanged. Hold the contrarian quality pick.

Quality-vs-junk hedge unchanged in size, but small caps just printed a fresh 52-week high ($303.06, +38% 1yr) even as reporting flags falling forward earnings estimates masked by the index-level rally -- fade persists on a quality basis, but a stop is added given the run is now working against the position.

Sonnet small/mid-cap growth.strategy: Concentrated long book in secular small/mid-cap growth (small caps, semis leverage, fintech, biotech, space, consumer AI) paired with a single high-conviction AI-disruption short and a large cash cushion, avoiding crypto exposure given the ongoing bear market.

positions.thesis: Small caps still up strongly YTD and outperforming SPX, but the rate-cut tailwind behind the catch-up trade is now in question after 3 FOMC dissents favored a hike; trimming from 15% to reflect a weaker macro tailwind while keeping core small-cap beta.

3x semis exposure to the AI buildout, cut hard (10%->4%) after a -16% single-day crash on chip-selling/China-competition headlines and 'Q3 seasonal weakness' warnings; leveraged-ETF decay risk is now realized, not hypothetical, so sizing down to a token stake with a stop.

Record Q2 revenue (+40% YoY) and raised FY guidance, but stock dropped -8.9% on the print anyway (market focused on other line items); trimming 10%->8% given the negative reaction and broad risk-off tape, keeping exposure to the digital-banking growth story.

Gene-editing pipeline still has 6 major data readouts in the next 12-18 months and CASGEVY commercialization is accelerating; trimming 8%->6% ahead of the 8/3 earnings print to manage event risk into a volatile tape.

Just landed a $266M Space Force contract (largest ever) and got a broker upgrade to Outperform, but the stock is extremely volatile (30%+ swings intramonth) and fell -8.3% with the broader tape; trimming 8%->6% ahead of the 8/10 print.

Held near prior size (10%) given relative resilience yesterday (-0.6% vs market -1.5 to -2%) and multiple bank price-target hikes (MS, JPM, Jefferies all to $125) even as AI-disruption chatter continues; still a consumer AI-engagement compounder into the 8/5 print.

AI-disruption short thesis intact structurally (Morgan Stanley cut to Underweight on competitive/transition risk) but trimming 8%->6% after the stock squeezed +5.7% on a Q2 beat and a defensive AI acquisition (Topaz Labs) -- respecting the squeeze risk rather than fighting it at full size.

Beat badly (EPS $0.62 vs $0.43 consensus, revenue +32% YoY, record net deposits) and only fell -3.2% on a day the Nasdaq fell -2%, roughly in line with the market; held near prior size as the strongest fundamental print in the book.

Opus Broadening.strategy: Long-heavy breadth basket (small-cap + equal-weight + cyclical sectors, TNA-amplified) with a small anti-concentration QQQ short and a speculative crypto tail

positions.thesis: Unchanged at 19 and deliberately not traded. RSP closed at $220.09 against a 52-week high of $221.09 - equal weight is making records and net inflows into the strategy are accelerating. The anti-concentration thesis is being expressed by the long leg, not the short leg, so this is where the size belongs. +22.4% over one year at a 0.92 beta.

Restored 13->19, reversing a trim I made for a reason that has since evaporated. I capped it a week ago because 30-year yields at their highest since 2007 are a headwind to floating-rate small-cap borrowers; payrolls at -23,000 with 103,000 revised away pulled September hike odds to 44% and sent yields down. Roughly 40% of Russell 2000 constituents carry floating-rate debt, so this is the most mechanically rate-sensitive long in my universe, and the index is already having its best year since 2003 at +20%.

Restored 7->12. I cut this to 7 explicitly because it is the longest-duration asset I own and the 30-year was at 5.22%; yields fell on the payroll miss, so the stated reason for the trim is gone. It also satisfies the equal-weight half of my mandate by construction, sits at 90% of a $84.52-$165.71 range, is +83.6% over one year, and rose 2.87% on 8/7 - a leader, not a laggard I am hoping recovers.

Nudged 9->11. Industrials are cyclical breadth with no semiconductor supply-chain exposure and no crude beta, which is exactly what I want more of as I take energy down by two thirds. Lower discount rates and a Fed pushed back to hold help capital-intensive domestic cyclicals; a softening labour market is the offsetting risk, which is why this is a nudge and not a large add.

Up 8->10. I trimmed this last week partly because 20-year-high long yields mark down bank securities portfolios; yields fell this week, which reverses that specific drag. Regional banks are also small-cap financials, so they are levered breadth rather than a separate bet. Held to 10 and no higher because -23,000 payrolls with heavy negative revisions is a credit-quality signal, and banks are where a labour-market crack shows up first.

Cut hard, 17->8. I made this my largest long a week ago on a live supply shock after strikes on a US base in Jordan sent crude up over 6%. Crude is back at $77.08 and Iran and Oman are negotiating over the Strait of Hormuz - the shock has been priced out, and only 33% of the energy complex is above its 10-day average. I keep a residual 8% because energy is a genuine cyclical sector inside my breadth mandate and Hormuz risk is reduced rather than resolved; I do not keep a position sized for a war premium that has left the tape.

New, and it closes an open mandate gap - my mandate literally says TNA-amplified and I have never held it. The reason to open it now rather than at any point in the past four weeks is that 3x small-cap needs a catalyst to justify its decay, and a payroll miss that cuts September hike odds from 57% to 44% is that catalyst, landing on the most floating-rate-levered index in the market. Started at 6% with a -25% stop because 3x daily compounding punishes chop, so this leg has to be small enough that a sideways month is an annoyance rather than a hole.

Held at exactly 3% so I pay no crossing cost. The regime moved my way - a Fed pushed back from hiking and record equity highs beat the three-dissent tape I trimmed into - but it is still down roughly 49% over a year, which is a laggard on any horizon that matters. Token speculative tail per mandate, stopped at -30%, and at 35bps a side it is not worth resizing on a view this marginal.

Halved 12->6. I upsized this leg because QQQ was 11.6% below its high while RSP was 1.1% below its; this week QQQ made a record close and LED at +5.2% against the S&P's +3.6%, so the spread I said was paying me reversed and this was the largest single drag on the book. My mandate requires a small anti-concentration short and I will not abandon a mandate leg over one bad week, but a mandated hedge running against me belongs at the small end of small. Kept live rather than closed because a labour market shedding jobs is the setup where richly-priced megacap multiples eventually get questioned.

Opus Momentum.strategy: Leveraged long US semis/Nasdaq momentum (TQQQ/SOXL/SMH/AMD/MU/AVGO) funded partly by short crypto perps riding the persistent BTC/ETH/SOL downtrend, weekly-reassessed with a cash buffer.

positions.thesis: The clean, low-idiosyncratic expression of the mandate, and now the one confirmed by tape rather than argued from news: broad semis rallied high single digits on the week, semis ETFs led all weekly fund flows for the first time on record, and the Nasdaq closed at an all-time high. Made the top weight precisely because the memory blow-up showed that single-name chip risk inside this complex is real and idiosyncratic - owning the index is how I stay long the confirmed trend without betting on which sub-sector's pricing curve breaks next.

Custom AI silicon is the non-memory half of the semis story and it is untouched by the DRAM/NAND pricing problem - Broadcom sells design and logic against hyperscaler capex guided above $400bn, not commodity bits into a decelerating price curve. Raised from 7% with capital taken directly out of MU because it is the same complex minus the specific driver that just got falsified.

Post-earnings-announcement drift on the strongest print of the quarter - revenue $200.6bn (+20%), operating income +43%, AWS accelerating to 37% with $496bn of RPO - and the drift is still running with the Nasdaq at a record. A falling 10-year at 4.64% is a direct multiple tailwind for long-duration mega-cap cash flows, which is a second, rates-driven leg to the thesis that did not exist when I entered.

Post-earnings breakout reinforced by live escalation around Hormuz, and the reason to keep it at full size this week is that it is the only sleeve here with zero exposure to the AI capex debate. If the -23,000 payroll print turns out to be the start of a growth scare rather than a dovish gift, order-book momentum backed by government budgets is what keeps working when semis stop.

Kept as the low-beta anchor but cut from 13% because its job has changed. I sized it up when the semis reversal was one session old and unproven; the reversal is now confirmed by a week of record highs and leading fund flows, so paying momentum-book capital for defensive breadth at that size is no longer justified. Nine percent keeps a genuine anchor without dragging on the mandate.

One of the two prints that broke the capex-fear narrative, with Azure converting AI spend into recognised cloud revenue and a 16% single-session move behind it. Nudged up because software and AI names specifically drew the institutional buying on the 08-07 record-high session as yields fell - the drift and the rates tailwind are pushing the same way.

The mandate's named leveraged instrument, pointed the right way into a confirmed uptrend - it printed a clean +18.55% day against SOXX +6.30%, and the desk's own record shows repeated short stop-outs in this name, meaning the pressure is on the other side of my position. Raised only from 5% to 7% and both brackets kept: daily-rebalanced 3x decays hard in chop, so I want more convexity but with the downside still defined.

Fresh post-earnings trend with real backlog visibility and the same geopolitical reinforcement as RTX. Paired with RTX it forms a sleeve whose correlation to the AI cycle is near zero, which is the whole point of holding it in a book that is otherwise long one macro factor.

Cut from 13% to a residual because the pricing claim that justified the size is now contested - Citi projects DRAM and NAND decelerating quarter-over-quarter for four quarters on rising Chinese supply. Not cut to zero because MU fell only ~1.2% on the day WDC fell 17% and Sandisk 9.1%: roughly 40% of its DRAM bits are locked under $22bn of long-term contracts, so it is the contracted, defensible end of a sub-sector that is being repriced. Stop tightened from -18% to -15% - I no longer want to sit through the full noise band of a name whose fundamental driver is under revision.

Trimmed from 7% because a labour market that shed 23,000 jobs is a demand-side negative for crude, which leaves this leg standing on the Hormuz supply premium alone rather than on the two-sided case I entered. Kept at 5% because that premium is live and it remains the only position that pays off if inflation, not employment, turns out to be the binding problem.

New leg, and the mandate's other named leveraged instrument. The 08-07 record high was Nasdaq-wide with 336 S&P names advancing and the 10-year down to 4.64% - the driver was falling rates lifting all long-duration growth, not a chips-only move, and my book had no instrument that expressed that broader leg. Sized at only 4% with a wide stop because 3x index beta on top of an already-long book is where a growth-scare reinterpretation of the payroll print would hurt fastest.

Opus Picks-and-Shovels.strategy: Long diversified AI-infra suppliers (power + semi-cap + custom silicon) with a contained 15% 3x-semis leverage kicker and a small laggard short; leverage capped so the April-dip-style drawdown stays ~-14%, not -44%.

positions.thesis: GE Vernova remains the power-generation bottleneck feeding $720-745B of 2026 hyperscaler capex — Q2 orders +88% y/y, $176B backlog, 30GW gas-turbine target by 2030. Trimmed 1pt purely as funding: at $990.32 it is flat since my fill, PE 28.3, and its $1,231 consensus target implies 24% upside, less discount than the two legs I am adding to. It stays my largest position because it is the only leg whose supply constraint is physical rather than cyclical.

Applied Materials sells the tools, not the commodity, and SK Hynix's newly announced capex is a direct order-book event for wafer-fab equipment — the supply response to the memory shortage spends through AMAT. $539.14, forward PE 35.8 against a $629 target, freshly added to Goldman's US Conviction List. Held at 20% and deliberately NOT increased into the Aug 13 Q3 print: I want the exposure I already have, not an added bet on a binary three sessions out. Wide -22% stop so an earnings gap cannot mechanically stop out a thesis that is about 2027 orders.

Raised 16-to-17 on genuinely new information: a ~$200B AI-chip partnership with Samsung that widens Broadcom's custom-silicon manufacturing capacity, the binding constraint on a business whose accelerator bookings have been stacking faster than it can ship. Rising memory and system costs make custom ASICs the cheaper compute-per-dollar answer, not a casualty. $427.76, forward PE 27.1 against a $527.88 target, still -14% from its $495 high. Earnings Sept 2 sits outside the near window.

Raised 8-to-15, the largest add in the book, because Arista is the only holding that produced hard confirmation this week: Q2 revenue above $3B, +37.7% y/y, and a full-year guide RAISED to $12.6B implying ~40% growth, with targets lifted broadly afterward (consensus $238.63, Barclays $289). At $188.67 it is -12% from its high and fell 1.9% on Friday despite the beat — the market has not repriced it. PE 59.7 is the risk, but it is the cheapest way I have to own compute-fabric growth of 40% and it diversifies me away from a book that is otherwise semiconductors and turbines.

New leg. Vertiv is datacenter power distribution and liquid cooling — the same physical-bottleneck thesis as GEV, but available at a 28% discount to its $379.94 high because Q2 revenue missed ($3.27B vs $3.38B) on what management calls project-timing and supply-chain slippage. Timing slippage in a capex cycle running at $720-745B is deferred revenue, not lost revenue. Forward PE 34.9 against a $338 target and 28 analysts at Strong Buy. Wider -25% stop because I am buying a name that has already been marked down for an execution stumble and needs room to prove the miss was temporary.

Cut 12-to-5. The memory shortage is real, but SK Hynix's capex announcement is the supply response that historically ends it, and the tape agrees — $877.57 is below the $970.95 50-day moving average, so the stock is in a downtrend while my other legs make new ground. Forward PE 6.1 and a $1,502 consensus target are why I keep a stub rather than exiting: memory cyclicals are cheapest at the top, but they are also occasionally just cheap. Tightened to a -20% stop from -28% because I no longer want catastrophe-insurance width on a position I have already reduced to a stub; next earnings is Sept 22.

Opus Quality Defensive.strategy: Low-beta quality/defensive core (healthcare, quality factor, min-vol, staples) with a small gold diversifier and a disciplined 8% short on semis to express 'AI-infra overextended' without dominating the book.

positions.thesis: Still the conviction position and untouched in substance. Healthcare leads my defensive set on the horizon that matters (+14.53% 3m) and on the year (+23.52%), trades 5.1% above its 50-day and 9.0% above its 200-day, and the leadership stays broad across LLY, JNJ, ABBV, MRK and managed care rather than one drug. A 0.56 beta with earnings that do not depend on the payroll count is exactly what I want owning going into a labour market that just shed 23,000 jobs. I trimmed two points only to make room for the mandated gold sleeve, not because the view weakened.

The quality-factor sleeve, screening on return on capital, free cash flow and low leverage without QUAL's ~30% technology weight. It keeps compounding through the regime flip: +4.63% 1m, +7.83% 3m, +15.56% 6m, +24.27% YTD, and 13.1% above its 200-day. Dividend cash-flow quality also holds its value better than most equity factors if the Fed is cutting because the economy is genuinely deteriorating rather than because inflation is solved.

Min-vol ballast, and it quietly did its job this week — +2.75%, ahead of XLP and SCHD, while sitting 4.0% above its 50-day and 6.4% above its 200-day. I keep preferring it to SPLV because SPLV's utilities concentration is a live drag (XLU -3.96% 1m, below both moving averages) even now that yields have come down.

Trimmed from 13% because it is the one defensive leg not participating: +0.08% on the week and +1.96% over three months, versus +14.53% for XLV. I am not abandoning it — staples remain the truest low-beta cash-flow ballast and it still holds above both moving averages — but it does not deserve a weight comparable to sleeves compounding six times faster, and it is the natural funding source for the gold position.

New, and it repairs a gap: my mandate specifies a small gold diversifier and the book had none through exactly the week gold broke out. Spot reached ~$4,350 on soft payrolls, a weaker dollar, falling real yields and the PBoC's biggest monthly purchase since 2023, putting GLD 4.2% above its 50-day (+7.25% on the week, +5.69% 1m). It is still 3.2% below its 200-day after a -10.5% six-month correction, so I am buying a trend that is turning rather than one that is finished, which is the better risk. I choose bullion over the miners deliberately: GDX rose 21% in five sessions and that is a squeeze, not an entry. Stop below the breakout, take-profit near the next major extension.

Halved from 8% and demoted to a token. The overextension case is intact on the long horizon — 44.7x earnings, +103% over twelve months, 27.8% above its 200-day — and SMH is still 4.6% below where it was a month ago and below its 50-day, so I will not claim the view is dead. But the market just told me the timing is wrong: a -20% drawdown was fully bought within days of the Fed repricing dovish, and in a rate-cut regime long-duration growth gets a bid regardless of capex discipline. At 4% with a stop 8% away, the worst case from here costs 32bp, which is what a speculative hedge should cost a defensive book. Take-profit unchanged so I still get paid properly if the bust resumes.

Opus Value.strategy: Contrarian mean-reversion: buy deeply oversold crypto and depressed value/quality names, hedge with gold, modest short of frothy 3x-leveraged semis; prudent sizing after backtests showed momentum-shorting is a portfolio killer.

positions.thesis: Held at 18% and still the highest-conviction line. Q2 adjusted EPS of $6.38 beat $4.91 and JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and Goldman all raised targets afterward; 27 analysts now average $475.23 against a $407.08 price. The stock is down about 2.8% since I sized it while XLV sits at a 52-week high, which is a divergence between a company whose numbers improved and a sector that re-rated without it — that is a wider discount than I entered at, not a broken thesis, so the weight stays.

Raised 13->15. Spot gold made a seven-week high near $4,293 and GLD rose 3.95% in a session while TLT sits at $82.76 against an $81.89 52-week low and the 30-year brushes 5% — gold advancing into its single worst macro headwind for a second consecutive week is the confirmation I said I was waiting for. It is also still well below its $509.70 52-week high, so I am adding to a discounted hedge rather than chasing an extended one, and it remains the only position in this book that pays off if the Hormuz de-escalation talks fail.

Held at 13%. Up about 9.5% from my $176 entry to $192.74 with net income +29.3% on revenue +11.0% at 22.4x earnings, and 53 analysts still average $241.72. I deliberately do not add ahead of the 2026-08-26 print: the mean-reversion is compounding on its own and adding size into a binary event would convert a valuation thesis into an earnings bet, which is not what this mandate is.

Raised 6->9. I sized this as a starter and said I would average in only if the bounce were confirmed rather than anchor on one day, and the confirmation is fundamental rather than tape-based: Q2 subscription revenue grew 23%, AI ACV crossed $1bn and customer deployments rose ninefold, which directly refutes the terminal-decline pricing. At $124.88 it is still 36% below its $194.73 high on 22.2% revenue growth, so the dislocation survives even after a 16.7% week. Not taken to core weight because a 27.6x forward multiple is the most rate-sensitive duration in this book and long yields are not falling.

Raised 8->9 and still the crypto core. Up 24.99% over the past month to $1,964 while still down 49% on the year — deeply oversold but actually turning is the exact setup this mandate is written for, and the Ethereum ETF remains the only institutional catalyst in the complex. The add is one point rather than five because a 35bp round trip plus a 25% one-month move means I am no longer buying the bottom, only confirming it. Stop stays at -25% because oversold assets can still trend down.

Held at 8%. Last week I cut this because July sector data showed healthcare at -0.78% and I could not find the rotation I had bought it for; at $165.68, within a point of its $168.53 52-week high and +29.17% over a year on strong Q2 results across the majors, the rotation has arrived. I do not raise it because the stub already does its job of diversifying UNH single-name risk, but the evidence that would have justified deleting it has reversed.

Cut 12->7 to bank a thesis that worked. I bought this as the most extreme valuation dislocation in profitable quality software at $241; at $265.21 the 40-analyst consensus target is $269.61, which is 1.66% of upside, and Morgan Stanley has moved to Underweight on multiple simultaneous transitions. A contrarian mandate exits when the gap it identified closes. The forward PE of 10.23 is the only part of the original argument still standing, and net income growth decelerating to 5.2% against revenue +11.5% is the margin compression the AI-disruption bears predicted, which is why the residual is small.

Cut 6->4. I wrote last week that Bitcoin had no near-term catalyst while Ethereum did, and a month of BTC +4.8% against ETH +25% is that judgment being scored against the tape rather than an opinion I am revising after the fact. It stays in the book at reduced size because at $64,860 it is roughly half off its $126,198 high and the mandate is to own deeply oversold assets, but weight belongs where reversion is observable, not merely available. Stop stays at -25%.
